logline: An orphaned girl moves in with a family whose members transform into Chinese zodiac animals when embraced by someone of the opposite sex, and becomes determined to break the ancient curse binding them.

renewal.note: The three-season remake ran April 2019 to June 2021, completing the full manga story. TMS Entertainment confirmed the story is concluded with Season 3 (Fruits Basket: The Final).

bollymeter.basis: 96% Rotten Tomatoes from critics, with consensus praising its ensemble depth and emotional range. IMDb audience score of 8.5 reflects consistent cross-demographic appeal.

pull_quotes.text: With such a large and likable ensemble cast, the diversity of life experiences means nearly any viewer can find something to relate to.

seasons.review_body: The 2019 remake of Fruits Basket aired April 6 to September 21, 2019, produced by TMS Entertainment. It won a 96 percent Rotten Tomatoes score, with critics at Common Sense Media and The Mary Sue praising the ensemble and the show's emotional honesty. Princess Weekes at The Mary Sue called it definitely worth your time. The series is a full-story adaptation unlike the 2001 version, allowing it to develop the darker psychological currents of the source manga. The IMDb audience rating of 8.5 reflects a broad viewer consensus that the remake delivered on the premise's potential. The first season establishes all its key relationships while hinting at the generational trauma that drives the later arcs.

episode_reviews.title: Spring Wind
episode_reviews.review_body: Fruits Basket's 2019 remake premiere aired April 6, 2019 on TBS and established itself within its first episode as something distinctly different from the 2001 adaptation. Studio TMS Entertainment brought a fuller budget and production standard that Funimation's simulcast carried internationally; the premiere's character animation and background art were immediately cited as among the strongest in the Spring 2019 season. Writer Taku Kishimoto's adaptation of Natsuki Takaya's manga established Tohru Honda with warmth and precision - a character whose relentless positivity was framed not as a personality quirk but as a survival mechanism, which the premiere understood without naming. The Sohma household's supernatural conceit - members of the family transform into animals of the Chinese zodiac under specific conditions - was introduced with the premiere's tonal intelligence intact: the transformation sequence was played for both comedy and sudden sadness simultaneously, a register the series sustained across three seasons and 63 episodes. The 100 percent Rotten Tomatoes score across all three seasons reflected a critical consensus that the remake had taken its source material seriously from the premiere.
episode_reviews.spoiler_free: The premiere introduces Tohru Honda and the Sohma household with warmth and precision. The central supernatural conceit is established without losing sight of the emotional truth underneath - the isolation each Sohma carries.
episode_reviews.the_moment: The first transformation scene, played for both comedy and sudden sadness simultaneously.

bollymeter.basis: 94% Rotten Tomatoes. Critics noted the season deepened the Sohma family trauma arcs and romance development substantially beyond Season 1.

pull_quotes.text: An anime gem that provides better emotional support and romantic triumphs than any horoscope.

seasons.review_body: Season 2 aired April 7 to September 22, 2020, again produced by TMS Entertainment. It earned a 94 percent Rotten Tomatoes score, with Fotogramas calling it an anime gem that provides better emotional support than any horoscope. Critics agreed that this season sharpened the show's engagement with abuse, generational trauma, and codependency in a way that elevated it beyond typical shojo fare. The sustained pace of emotional revelation across 25 episodes kept audiences invested, and the romantic threads between Tohru and Kyo grew more complex.
seasons.season_over_season: Deepens the psychological and romantic layers established in Season 1; the villain's backstory receives meaningful screen time and shifts the moral stakes.

bollymeter.basis: 100% Rotten Tomatoes from available critics. Audiences rated the finale arc highly for emotional resolution, though some noted the handling of the antagonist's redemption arc as divisive.

pull_quotes.text: Fruits Basket is caught in a weird in-between, where we're expected to feel sympathy for Akito, even though she faces no repercussions.

seasons.review_body: The Final season ran April 6 to June 29, 2021, across 13 episodes, concluding the full story of the Sohma curse and Tohru's relationships. The sole Rotten Tomatoes critical entry rated it 100 percent, though Polygon noted the show's ambivalence toward its central antagonist's redemption as a genuine tension in the finale arc. Audiences embraced the emotional payoffs for the central romance, and the conclusion to the curse's mythology. The condensed 13-episode run maintained energy while sacrificing some of the slower character beats that defined Seasons 1 and 2.
seasons.season_over_season: Compresses the ending into 13 episodes; emotionally satisfying for the central romance, though the antagonist's resolution divided viewers who wanted stronger consequences.
